title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - description 
 description : The Aldrich Faithfuls protect Lord Aldrich from harmful ash, such as the Ashen One, and claim Human Dregs as their prizes. These may be used to rank up in the covenant for rewards.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : To join the Aldrich Faithful covenant, the player must first have cleared the area by defeating both Sulyvahn's Beasts and then proceed to Archdeacon McDonnell's remains and pray to them, at this point they may ask to join and obtain proof of the covenant.

Killing the Sulyvahn's beasts is not required to join the covenant. If one wears the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring and casts Hidden Body just as they reach the bottom of the ladder, they can sneak around the left, far wall and avoid the beasts and pray to McDonnell, thus joining.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Aldrich Faithful** is a covenant in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Like the Watchdogs of Farron, Aldrich Faithful will be called upon to defend Aldrich's territory from trespassers; any player who has Host of Embers status will be subject to invasion. This area is defined as anywhere from the courtyard upon exiting Pontiff Sulyvahn's arena, up until the rotating stairway leading up to Anor Londo. Aldrich Faithful can pursue trespassers up into the cathedral itself, but will not be summoned for trespassers who have already reached the upper level bonfire.

Defeating the Host of Embers will reward all present Aldrich Faithful with Human Dregs, which can be offered to Archdeacon McDonnell to deepen their allegiance to the covenant.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - location 
 location : The Aldrich Faithful covenant can be found in the lower plane of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed onward and make way to the other side of the large courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Upon entering the main building on the opposite side, hit the wall on the left to reveal an illusory wall concealing the main access to the covenant.

Climb down the large ladder to reach a big, flooded hall. There are two Sulyvahn's Beasts lying in wait once reaching this area, one on the left and one further ahead on the right.

In one corner of the room lie the remains of Archdeacon McDonnell. Interacting with him allows access into the covenant.

title: Aldrich Faithful (item)
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful (item) -  Dark Souls III - item - lead 
 lead : **Aldrich Faithful** (神喰らいの守り手) is a covenant item in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Aldrich Faithful (item)
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful (item) -  Dark Souls III - item - description 
 description : The holy symbol of the Cathedral of the Deep, and crest of those who see beyond fire to the age of deep waters. Equip to pledge oneself to the Aldrich Faithful covenant.

The faithful ensure that Aldrich, Devourer of Gods, remains undisturbed, by taking the form of loyal spirits and hunting down those who would trespass the ruined cathedral.

Summoning takes place automatically while this is equipped.

title: Aldrich Faithful (item)
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful (item) -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Found in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Obtained by interacting with Archdeacon McDonnell's remains in the Water Reserve and accepting to join the Aldrich Faithful covenant.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed through the level and make way to the opposite side of the big courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Enter the building at the end and hit the wall on the left to reveal a hidden ladder. Climb down and defeat the two Sulyvahn's Beasts lurking at the bottom. Once done, head to the far-left corner of the room to find McDonnell's remains.

title: Aldrich Faithful (item)
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful (item) -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Equip to pledge oneself to the Aldrich Faithful covenant. Summoning takes place automatically while this item is equipped.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet: After Aldrich linked the Flame, a cult formed around his figure, but the deacons of the cathedral also found themselves fighting abominations that emerged from the Deep. The Cathedral, once a peaceful and sacred place for purification, was corrupted by the foul Aldrich, as darkness stagnated and accumulated in the Deep until it had become the final rest of abhorrent creatures. McDonnell found delight in the stagnation of darkness and abandoned his faith in the First Flame and in the gods, devoting himself to the Deep. He spread his belief among the clerics of the cathedral; he even created staffs that channeled faith to produce Deep sorceries, a sacrilegious act. In time the cathedral's deacons became both clergymen and sorcerers, embracing the cult of the Deep and the worship of its Saint, Aldrich.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : McDonnell, along with Archdeacons Royce and Klimt, was an archdeacon of the Way of White. The three men managed the Cathedral of the Deep, overseeing its rituals of purification from stagnant Darkness.

At one point, the cathedral welcomed Aldrich, an exiled Irithyllian priest who derived pleasure from eating humans. Aldrich shared his perverse behaviour with others in the cathedral, and sacrifices were brought to him to appease his hunger and grant him the strength to link the First Flame and become a Lord of Cinder.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - location 
 location : Archdeacon McDonnell's remains can be found in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, at the Water Reserve.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed onward until reaching the building at the end of the big courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Upon entering, hit the left wall to uncover an illusory wall. Descend the ladder and dispose of the two Sulyvahn's Beasts waiting at the bottom. Archdeacon McDonnell's remains are located at the far-left corner of the hall, near the Water Reserve bonfire, which will appear once both beasts have been defeated.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : **Archdeacon McDonnell**, or **McDonnell of the Boreal Valley**, is a character in *Dark Souls III*. Praying to his remains allows access to the Aldrich Faithful covenant.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet: At some point McDonnell was incapacitated and his body ended up in the lower levels of Irithyll, in a cistern guarded by two of Pontiff Sulyvahn's beasts, however he is still able to recognize others, as he manages Aldrich's covenant and teaches sorceries.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : Archdeacon McDonnell, a sorcerer himself, delighted in the cathedral's stagnating souls. For him, they represented the glorious bedrock of this world.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

Once Aldrich defeated Sulyvahn and took control of the city, McDonnell remained to watch over the old Cathedral where the saint was busy digesting Gwyndolin, establishing the covenant of Aldrich Faithful, passing on his dark sorceries to followers who brought him evidence of success in their task.

title: Bell Keeper of Alken
snippet:
Bell Keeper of Alken -  Dark Souls II - character - locations 
 locations : Just after the door that leads to Belfry Luna.
Just before the fog door that leads to Belfry Sol.

title: Bell Keeper of Alken
snippet:
It is likely that Venn once stood where Belfy Sol does; as Belfry Sol, which the Bell Keeper calls "Arken", is atop the Iron Keep, it is possible that the Prince was a member of the Old Iron King's family, perhaps the Old Iron King himself as he was in a loveless marriage to Mytha because he "had feelings for another". The original goal of the Bell Keepers might have been to somehow preserve the love affair between the Old Iron King and the Princess of Ven, or its memory.

It is unclear if the Bell Keeper Dark Spirit that can invade the player in Belfry Luna is the same as the Bell Keeper NPC; unlike the regular Bell Keeper enemies, who wear full helmets, the invader wears the same partial helmet as the NPC that lets most of his face apparent.

title: Bell Keeper of Alken
snippet:
Bell Keeper of Alken -  Dark Souls II - character - lead 
 lead : For the enemy that can be found in the same locations, see Bell Keeper (enemy). For the invading Dark Spirit in Belfry Luna, see Bell Keeper (Dark Spirit)*.
The **Bell Keeper of Alken**, also known as the **Bell Keeper of Venn**, is a character in *Dark Souls II*. He is voiced by Jason Pitt, who also voiced Vengarl of Forossa, Satsuki in *Demon's Souls* and Valtr, Master of the League in *Bloodborne*.

The leader of the Bell Keepers covenant, he can found in both areas protected by its members, Belfry Luna and Belfry Sol.

title: Bell Keeper of Alken
snippet:
Bell Keeper of Alken -  Dark Souls II - character - plot 
 plot : He is the leader of Bell Keepers covenant, which the player can join by talking to him. He will also provide rewards upon ranking up in the covenant. He also warns the player not to touch the bell he's protecting, or his minion will chop them to pieces.

Because the Bell Keeper has little sanity, it is unclear how much his dialogue can be trusted, but it hints that there might in fact be two distinct Bell Keepers, one in Luna and one and Sol, as in Luna he will claim that "the Princess" made him "To guard the Bell of Alken! In Alken!" while, in Sol, he claims that "the Prince" made him, "To guard the Bell of Venn! In Venn!". Killing the Bell Keeper in either location leads to the absence of the Bell Keeper from the other, further hinting at a direct connection and possibly towards them being the same person.

title: Bell Keeper's Seal
snippet:
Bell Keeper's Seal -  Dark Souls II - ring - lead 
 lead : The **Bell Keeper's Seal** is a ring in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Bell Keeper's Seal
snippet:
Bell Keeper's Seal -  Dark Souls II - ring - description 
 description : Ring of the Bell Keeper covenant.

Join this covenant and wear this ring to be automatically summoned to the world of an invader of the bell keepers' domain.

The twin bells symbolize the bond between two lovers who could never be united. The bell keepers are their eternal guardians. For that is their love; that is their curse.

title: Bell Keeper's Seal
snippet:
Bell Keeper's Seal -  Dark Souls II - ring - effect 
 effect : Wearing this ring allows the player to invade another player who is either in Belfry Luna or Belfry Sol. Anyone's world can be invaded by a Bell Keeper, included fellow covenant members' worlds.

If worn in one of the belfries, the player will only invade trespassers in the same belfry as they currently are.

title: Bell Keeper's Seal
snippet:
Bell Keeper's Seal -  Dark Souls II - ring - availability 
 availability : Given to the player by the head Bell Keeper upon joining the Bell Keepers covenant.

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Bell Keepers -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : After joining the covenant and receiving the ring, the player will automatically invade other worlds while they are wearing it. The player does not need to be in either belfry to be eligible for summoning, they can be almost anywhere in the world other than Majula and Things Betwixt, as denoted by the Bell Keepers' badge on the heads-up display with a glowing effect animation.

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Bell Keepers -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Usually the members of the Bell Keepers covenant will invade players with ease and they tend to bunch up, to a maximum number of three, frequently outnumbering the host. At this point either two things happen: the Bell Keepers decide to work together and will most likely kill the player; or they battle each other for the host kill.
Though you can be summoned as gray spirit from any area in the world, you have a much higher chance if you are inside Belfry or it's governing area (Lost Bastille or Iron Keep).

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Bell Keepers -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : To join the Bell Keepers, the player must speak to the Bell Keeper of Alken at the entrance of Belfry Luna or Belfry Sol. Exhausting his dialogue will allow the player to join the covenant and accepting will have them recieve the Bell Keeper's Seal.

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Achieving victories over other players in the belfries will cause a player in the Bell Keepers to advance in the covenant. Upon defeating a trespassing player, the Bell Keeper member will get sent back to their world with a Titanite Chunk. A member of the covenant can also gain victories by defeating a rarely-spawning enemy in Belfry Sol, named the Mad Warrior. This makes the Bell Keepers one of the few covenants that can be ranked up while in offline mode.

Ranking up in this Covenant is the only way to get access to the Sorcery Hidden Weapon.

title: Bell Keepers
snippet: The goal of the player while invading is to protect Belfry Luna and Belfry Sol from trespassers, including invading Blue Arbiter Spirits and summoned Phantoms. Despite being a part of the covenant, the player will still be invaded by other Bell Keeper members, and the dwarven protectors in these places are still hostile. However, while the player is invading, the enemies will be non-aggressive and any other Bell Keepers summoned to invade will be allies. All summoned Bell Keeper members will appear as grey phantoms, and up to two Bell Keeper phantoms (three in ) can be summoned at a time.

title: Bell Keepers
snippet:
Bell Keepers -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The are a PvP-oriented covenant in *Dark Souls II*, devoted to protecting Belfry Luna and Belfry Sol from other players.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Blade of the Darkmoon** (暗月の剣) is a PvP-oriented covenant in *Dark Souls*. Darkmoon Blades hunt those who have sinned.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - betrayal 
 betrayal : Entering Gwyn's Tomb to confront Gwyndolin counts as a betrayal and results in expulsion from the covenant. Destroying the illusion of Gwynevere while being part of the Blades of the Darkmoon will NOT cause Gwyndolin to expel the player from the covenant, but it will prevent the player from offering any more souvenirs of reprisal to Gwyndolin.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Blade of the Darkmoon is considered one of the more difficult covenants to master. Every person the player invades as a spirit of vengeance has likely had experience in PvP (since Indictments during an invasion are one of the few repeatable ways of gaining sin), and so will usually put up a tougher fight than people invaded by Darkwraiths. To make matters worse, people in Dark Anor Londo are likely to be duel-mongerers who kill Blades of the Darkmoon for sport or for souls. They very often have friendly summons with them.

However, the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant is very worthwhile. The Darkmoon Talisman has the best miracle adjust in the game, so any player who relies on miracles would benefit from joining this covenant; in turn, Darkmoon Blade is an excellent weapon buff. With patience and perseverance, players may yet reap the benefits of the Blade of the Darkmoon.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : First, acquire the Darkmoon Seance Ring in The Catacombs. Go to the bottom level of the rotating elevator in Anor Londo to find the Darkmoon Tomb bonfire. Past the bonfire, Gwyn's statue will disappear to reveal a fog gate if the player is wearing the Darkmoon Seance Ring. If the player has killed Gwynevere, the statue will just disappear when approached. Go toward the fog gate and Dark Sun Gwyndolin will ask the player to swear fealty to the Blades of the Darkmoon. Kneel at the fog door to join the covenant.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - activities 
 activities : Blades of the Darkmoon hunt players that have attacked the illusion of Gwynevere or have committed any amount of sins by either getting kicked out of a covenant or being indicted by other players. Players risk nothing invading other people's worlds (cannot be indicted and all souls and humanity are kept upon death) and gain a Souvenir of Reprisal for each guilty player they defeat.

Outside of Gwyndolin, the only character part of the covenant is the Anor Londo Fire Keeper, although she does not provide a fellow Darkmoon Blade with anything besides unique dialogue. Attacking Gwynevere or passing through Gwyndolin's fog gate will result in her turning hostile, but killing the Fire Keeper will not count as betraying the covenant.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - known_members 
 known_members : Darkmoon Knightess
Greatsword-wielding Darkmoon Soldier
Straight Sword-wielding Darkmoon Soldier

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Upon joining, players receive:
Blue Eye Orb
Darkmoon Blade Covenant Ring

Souvenirs of Reprisal are offered to Dark Sun Gwyndolin to gain ranks in the Blade of the Darkmoon Covenant.

Players may only use the Darkmoon Blade miracle when they are in the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant; the buff is initially 1.8x of the magic adjust of the talisman, but will gain 0.1 with every level gained in the covenant (1.9x at +1, 2.0x at +2, and 2.1x at +3).

Being part of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant does not prevent invasions from other members.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : The player must not have killed Dark Sun Gwyndolin. If the player has killed Gwynevere, they must request absolution from Oswald before joining.

title: Bloodbite Ring (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bloodbite Ring (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - ring - availability 
 availability : ***Bloodbite Ring**
** Purchased from Cromwell the Pardoner for 7,000 souls
** Received from Crestfallen Saulden after achieving Rank 1 in the Way of Blue covenant.
***Bloodbite Ring +1**
** Found in the Dragon's Sanctum area in Shulva, Sanctum City.

title: Bloodbite Ring (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bloodbite Ring (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - ring - lead 
 lead : The **Bloodbite Ring** is a ring in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Bloodbite Ring (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bloodbite Ring (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - ring - description 
 description : One of several "bite" rings, known for their peculiar design. Increases bleeding resistance.

The similar, oddly disturbing design of these rings suggests a common source. Whoever the master craftsman was, he clearly knew his trade.

title: Bloodbite Ring (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bloodbite Ring (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - ring - effects 
 effects : Regular version provides 150 Bleed resistance.
+1 version provides 300 Bleed resistance.

title: Blue Eye Orb
snippet:
Blue Eye Orb -  Dark Souls - item - availability 
 availability : Granted after joining the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant.

title: Blue Eye Orb
snippet:
Blue Eye Orb -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Online play item. Invade world of player in Book of the Guilty. Subdue player to acquire Souvenir of Reprisal. (Only Covenanter can use the item)

These mystical orbs are granted to Blades of the Darkmoon, knights who serve the Dark Sun Gwyndolin, so that they may serve the Gods in meting out vengeance.

title: Blue Eye Orb
snippet:
Blue Eye Orb -  Dark Souls - item - lead 
 lead : The **Blue Eye Orb** is an online play item in *Dark Souls*.

title: Blue Eye Orb
snippet:
Blue Eye Orb -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Using the Blue Eye Orb allows the player to attempt to invade the world of players that have been indicted. The player must be in the Blades of the Darkmoon covenant to use the Blue Eye Orb; unlike the Red Eye Orb, reversed hollowing is not required and a bloodstain is not left behind if the Blade of the Darkmoon is defeated. Upon defeat of the guilty player, the Blade of the Darkmoon will receive a Souvenir of Reprisal and the host's sin is reduced by 1.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to Blue Sentinel Targray, located in the Cathedral of Blue directly after the Old Dragonslayer boss fight. Reaching him before obtaining at least one Token of Fidelty will have him disregard the player, so be sure to find one if you wish to join the covenant. Upon meeting the requirements and accepting Targray's offer, players will be awarded the Guardian's Seal.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Talking to Blue Sentinel Targray after achieving rank 3 in the covenant will cause him to give the player his armor set.
As Rank increases, the blue aura that surrounds the player when invading will become more prominent.
Killing Targray will automatically kick you out of the covenant, but temporarily resurrecting him through his gravestone will let you rejoin the covenant.
While ordinary invaders receive souls by killing the host, the only way for Arbiter Spirits to gain souls is by killing phantoms and dark spirits summoned by or invading the host.
Winning the sparring arena counts towards ranking.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet: They shared lineage with the Way of Blue, which was not an organized religion but "a humble prayer" that spread organically amongst the needy, eventually growing to the point where the towering Cathedral of Blue was built in the heart of Heide, used by the Blue Sentinels as headquarters. The Sentinels were tasked with defending the apostles of Blue from evil spirits as well as traversing space and time via their eye orbs to punish the guilty, similar to their progenitor. Victorious knights were rewarded with miracles of the ancient gods of Anor Londo like Wrath of the Gods and Bountiful Sunlight that had been lost or jealously guarded elsewhere in Drangleic.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet: Despite Heide's fall, the Blue Sentinels continued to exert considerable influence in countries near Drangleic. In Volgen, a city ruled by the clerics of the Way of Blue, a group calling themselves Blue Sentinels wields significant power, and hold sway over who can engage in trading within the city. Albeit they are not confirmed to be authentic Blue Sentinels, the rule of Volgen by the Way of Blue suggests that the Sentinels are indeed present in the city, as a bottleneck on mercantile competition.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The is a PvP-oriented covenant in *Dark Souls II*, devoted to protecting members of the Way of Blue and invading worlds of those who have sinned. It operates much like the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant from *Dark Souls*.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lore 
 lore : The Blue Sentinels are direct descendants of the original Blade of the Darkmoon covenant that served Dark Sun Gwyndolin in Anor Londo. The Sentinels were amongst those who left Lordran and reached Drangleic, founding the civilization of Heide as its Knights. These knights still possess the Cracked Blue Eye Orbs, the worn remains of the Blue Eye Orbs granted to the Blades of the Darkmoon who served Gwyndolin to mete out the vengeance of the gods at the times of Anor Londo.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : After joining the covenant, Targray can teach the player the Duel Bow gesture, he also sells a few common weapons like the Halberd, healing items like the Monastery Charm, and the Holy Water Urns.
He also sells the miracles Heavenly Thunder and Emit Force.
The player receives the Guardian's Seal, which will allow them to be summoned as an Arbiter Spirit by Way of Blue covenant members in order to help them defeat the invader that triggered the summon. A Token of Fidelity will be rewarded after the invader has been killed.
Members of the covenant also have the ability to use Cracked Blue Eye Orbs to invade the worlds of the guilty.
With a Token of Fidelity, players can interact with the statues near the Blue Cathedral bonfire to enter a PvP arena to fight other members of the Blue Sentinels.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet: The civilization of Heide was at some point lost to rising sea levels. While large sections were reduced to half-submerged rubble, the upper sections and the Tower of Flame were left intact, which continued to host the Blue Sentinels. With Targray at the helm, the Sentinels maintained their watch over the apostles of Blue; they even took on new recruits, for whom the Heide Knights, the Old Knights and an Old Dragonslayer served as initiation into the covenant. Those who proved their mettle gained access to the covenant leader, and could use the Cracked Blue Eye Orbs they pillaged from the knights to enact divine vengeance against sinners.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - mechanics 
 mechanics : A Blue Sentinel invading a guilty player with the Cracked Blue Eye Orb seems to favor invading players generally below the player's Soul Memory.
**This contrasts the Brotherhood of Blood members, who generally invade players above their own Soul Memory using the Cracked Red Eye Orb.
The Blue Sentinel can also use the Guardian's Seal to assist players against invaders, as long as the invader isn't also an Arbiter Spirit.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : Players must have one Token of Fidelity in their possession, which can be obtained either by defeating a boss in another player's world as a phantom, or by finding one hidden away in Huntsman's Copse for those who are playing offline. Alternatively, they can be obtained in NG+ or when Heide's Tower of Flame is at Bonfire intensity 2 by burning a Bonfire Ascetic, as Dark Spirits resembling Blue Sentinels will spawn and drop a token each when slain.

title: Blue Tearstone Ring (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Blue Tearstone Ring (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - ring - effect 
 effect : Increases defense by 35% when health goes below 30%.

title: Blue Tearstone Ring (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Blue Tearstone Ring (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - ring - lead 
 lead : The **Blue Tearstone Ring** is a ring in *Dark Souls II*

title: Blue Tearstone Ring (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Blue Tearstone Ring (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - ring - availability 
 availability : Drop down from second floor in Belfry Luna. The ring will be in a metal chest on that floor.
Recieved from Crestfallen Saulden after achieving Rank 3 in the Way of Blue covenant.

title: Blue Tearstone Ring (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Blue Tearstone Ring (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - ring - description 
 description : A ring set with a blue tearstone.
Reacts when the wearer is in danger, temporarily increasing its wearer's physical defense power.

Caitha, goddess of tears, mourns those who have lost loved ones by shedding pure tears of blue.
It is said that the stone set in this ring is one such tear.

title: Cleric
snippet:
At an initial level of 2, Clerics have the second-lowest starting level (the lowest being Pyromancers) of any class. They start the game as a member of the Way of White covenant.

Joining the Warriors of Sunlight can allow Clerics to become powerful magical attackers early on in the game, giving them the miracle Lightning Spear. Astora's Straight Sword and Dragon Crest Shield are also very useful early game pick-ups for the Cleric, provided they choose the Master Key as their gift and enter Valley of Drakes via New Londo Ruins. The former scales with Faith, allowing the Cleric to focus exclusively on it, while the latter is a far better shield than that which the Cleric starts with.

title: Cleric
snippet:
Cleric -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Cleric** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls*.

Clerics can use miracles to heal, due to their high starting Faith stat and equipped Talisman. They also start with a strong melee weapon in the form of the Mace, but little in the way of defense. Clerics are well suited to heavier weapon types, such as Hammers, as taking on enemies directly with slower weapons is offset by their ability to heal more often than other classes.

At an initial level of 2, Clerics have the second-lowest starting level (the lowest being Pyromancers) of any class. They start the game as a member of the Way of White covenant.

title: Crestfallen Saulden
snippet:
Crestfallen Saulden -  Dark Souls II - character - comic_appearance 
 comic_appearance : Saulden appears as a central figure in the comic *Dark Souls II: Into the Light*.A lone warrior bearing a curse meets Saulden when the latter is resting at a bonfire. Saulden decides to invite the warrior to sit around the fire for a while. After a brief conversation, the undead warrior decides to continue his quest, although Saulden tries to convince him to stay for a little longer in order to share some of his knowledge with him. The warrior, however, refuses his offer, deeming that his sword "belongs to a crestfallen man who hides by his fire".

Soon, the same warrior returns, bloodied and dying. Using his blood, he desperately writes a summon sign into the ground before dying, his corpse fading away. Moments later, the warrior is reincarnated near the bonfire. Saulden then asks if the warrior will listen to his advice this time. The warrior replies with "I will."

title: Crestfallen Saulden
snippet:
Saulden invites the player to join the Way of Blue covenant, so that the Blue Sentinels can come to their aid whenever they are being targeted by Dark Spirits. Upon following him up on his offer, players will recieve the Blue Seal as well as the "**Covenant of the Meek**" Achievement. Furthermore, Saulden will reward players who join the covenant when they rank up by vanquishing invaders, be they players or hostile NPCs.

Upon dying one hundred times, Saulden will gift the player with a Ring of Steel Protection to help them on their journey. He will also gift the players with a Soul Vessel should they finish his small questline, which involves rounding up four different characters from around the kingdom. Doing so will give the broken knight some much-needed comfort. This side quest will also award the player with the "**Gathering of Exiles**" Achievement.

title: Crestfallen Saulden
snippet:
Crestfallen Saulden -  Dark Souls II - character - plot 
 plot : Saulden is a spiritual successor of the Crestfallen Warrior from the previous game and *Demon's Souls*. While he is still as depressed and hopeless as his predecessors, he seems to have a much friendlier personality, offering helpful advice to the player without belittling them. He is quite helpful for first-time players, as he reveals information about gameplay mechanics such as messages and summon signs, information about Drangleic and directions for where to go. Players can also learn the "**Welcome**" gesture from him upon going through his introduction speech.

title: Crestfallen Saulden
snippet:
Despite his pessimistic outlook on life and existence, he still has much faith in the Way of Blue, a humble religion spread among those who seek help. He seems to have been a follower even before his loss of will, since the Emerald Herald describes him as a "blue knight". He will let the Bearer of the Curse join the covenant if they ever feel overwhelmed and in need of assistance.

The Bearer of the Curse can eventually lead more people to Majula, which will lighten Saulden's mood and make him remember better times. Finding new peace in companionship, he'll feel gratitude towards the adventurer.

title: Crestfallen Saulden
snippet:
Crestfallen Saulden -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Saulden is a cursed Undead, much like the Bearer of the Curse and many who have found their way in Drangleic. Like them, he was expected to go on a perilous journey to find a way to end the Curse, but lost hope along the way, his spirit crushed by the trials of the ruined kingdom. As a result, he sits at the foot of the great monument of Majula, deep in contemplation, and he offers guidance to those who find their way to the seaside hamlet. He thinks it's hopeless to look for a cure for the Curse, since it originates from life and the soul itself.

title: Crestfallen Saulden

 location : He is encountered in Majula, sitting at the foot of its tall, obelix-like monument found atop a cliff just north of the village's bonfire. He remains there for the entire game.

title: Crestfallen Saulden
snippet:
Crestfallen Saulden -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : Saulden is the only "Crestfallen Warrior" in the *Dark Souls* series who doesn't die during his storyline, and instead finds some semblance of hope and peace.
When attacked and not made hostile, he will stop holding his usual pose and instead point forward disapprovingly.
He is the NPC with the longest wait for his grave to spawn but the cheapest cost for his spirit to be summoned back.
In early screenshots and in the comic, Saulden is seen wearing the Hard Leather Set from the first game, instead of the armor set that he wears in the final version of the game. This change of armor is probably due to the developers deciding Mild-Mannered Pate should be the owner of the set instead.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwyndolin is the lastborn child of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire, although his legitimacy as such only came from being a child of his father. He was worshipped as the "God of the Darkmoon" and held the title of "God of the Dark Sun".

Despite being the son of Gwyn, Gwyndolin was born with a strong moon power, and "weak and repulsive" in appearance, particularly due to the snakes coiled around his lower half. Because of his darkmoon powers and his strong affinity for moon magic, as well as his lineage, Gwyndolin was raised as a female. While still young, Gwyn made him wear women's clothing and gave him a magic ring which would allow Gwyndolin to move and act in a feminine way, leading him to behave "like a dark and fleeting goddess".

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Cut content from *Dark Souls III* reveals that it was possible to obtain a consumed finger of Gwyndolin, presumably after defeating Aldrich, and give it to Yorshka for her to keep as a memento.
In *Dark Souls*, 末子 is translated to lastborn, but in *Dark Souls 3* it is instead translated to its more accurate meaning of youngest son in the Darkmoon Ring description. This can call the canonicity of lastborn into question, as the difference doesn't exist in the original JP.
Gwyndolin is a derivative of the Welsh name "Gwendolyn" meaning "white ring"
**Among her namesakes, the legendary Queen of Britain Gwendolyn is particularly well-known, as depicted in "*Historia Regum Britanniae*" by Geoffrey of Monmouth, one of the oldest historiographers and authors of Arthurian Legend. Gwendolyn was renowned for her wisdom and grace in these tales.

The player can then either pledge allegiance to him and his Blades of the Darkmoon or dare to trespass the fog door behind which he dwells, thus commencing the boss battle.

title: Covenants (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Covenants (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Covenants are a staple in the *Dark Souls* franchise and online gameplay. Joining a covenant may change the parameters with which players connect to each other. The covenant the player is a part of will show with their nameplate to others and may cosmetically change the appearance of their phantom.

Each covenant has a specific function and goal the player must fulfill, and upon fulfilling that goal they are rewarded with a token specific to that covenant. All covenants have a character or altar where they may trade their tokens for certain prizes. One prize will be received after trading 10 tokens, another after trading 30 tokens. Participating in a covenant is all but required to obtain some weapons, spells, rings, etc.

title: Covenant
snippet:
Covenant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - changing_covenants 
 changing_covenants : Players may only join one covenant at a time. Should players wish to join a different covenant, it is necessary to break their contract with their previous covenant first, through betrayal, through Oswald, the pardoner, or by changing covenants at a bonfire (Remastered only). It is recommended to change covenants through Oswald, covenant leaders, or at a bonfire, as killing covenant leaders will often lead to much harsher penalties than simply changing covenants

Upon leaving a covenant, even with through Oswald, half of the progress the player has made in ranking up in the covenant is lost, should they wish to rejoin later. For example, having offered 30 humanity to a covenant will be reduced to 15 if one should rejoin and want to attain the previously held rank.

title: Covenant
snippet: It is possible to be kicked out of four of the covenants: Blade of the Darkmoon, Princess's Guard, Chaos Servant, and Forest Hunter. When kicked out of a covenant, any offerings made to that covenant will be reduced to 0 and requesting absolution will be required to rejoin the covenant, provided that the covenant leader is still alive.

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Duels from a Red Sign Soapstone do not count towards your rank.
Killing Gren will automatically kick you out of the covenant.
The Brotherhood of Blood was one of the three available covenants in the network test.
If one is not interested in dueling, the covenant rewards can be gotten in other ways:
**The Crest of Blood is obtained simply by joining the covenant.
**Gren will drop the Nahr Alma Hood upon death, and the Robes and Scythe will then be sold by Merchant Hag Melentia.
**Chancellor Wellager will sell the Curved Twinblade, Crescent Sickle, and Great Chaos Fireball in NG++.

title: Player versus Player (Dark Souls III)
snippet: The Blade of the Darmoon, Blue Sentinels and Spears of the Church covenant offer alternative ways to invade: the first two allow counter-invasions as a blue spirit to defend a currently-invaded player who is themselves a member of the Way of Blue covenant (therefore opening themselves to counter-invasions), while the third offers an opportunity to become a boss in *The Ringed City* DLC. Invasions can happen regardless of if the invaded player is willing, but fully consensual PvP also exists: the Red Sign Soapstone and the Champion's Bones both allow for such one-on-one duels, while the latter unlocks arena brawls. A certain number of non-playable character invasions can also occur, including in offline mode, effectively working like a player's.

title: Company of Champions
snippet:
Company of Champions -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Joining this covenant offers a higher degree of difficulty to the game and disables friendly summoning (including NPC summoning) and being summoned, although it is still possible to summon hostile spirits and be invaded. All enemies deal more damage and have increased defenses, although they won't actually have more health.
Defeating an invading red phantom will reward the player with an Awestone. Defeating red phantoms summoned through a Red Sign Soapstone won't yield Awestones. Certain enemies can also, rarely, drop Awestones. These Awestones can be offered to the Victor's Stone to rank up in the covenant.
Enemies gain higher tactical intelligence, as they will retreat when at low health and attack at the same time, making fighting multiple enemies much more dangerous.

title: Cat Covenant Ring
snippet:
Cat Covenant Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : The Cat Covenant Ring will add Forest Hunter players who wear it to an invasion queue. Those players will be sent to invade the worlds of non-Forest Hunter players who enter Darkroot Forest to kill them.

Unlike normal invasions, the Forest Hunter invasions can be performed even by hollow players and from anywhere in the game world (except for those areas without an associated boss, such as Firelink Shrine or Gwynevere's chamber in Anor Londo). There is no level restriction, meaning someone of low level such as 40 can invade anyone, so they could be paired with a level 200. The invaders lose nothing should they fail, including their non-hollowed state. Invaders who die will be returned to the last bonfire they visited with all items, souls, and humanity intact.

Removing the ring when in the target's world will not cause the player to return to their homeworld.

title: Pyromancy (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Pyromancy (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - spell - general_information 
 general_information : In *Dark Souls III*, pyromancies are aligned with both Faith and Intelligence. To cast a pyromancy, the player requires a Pyromancy Flame as a catalyst. The player can only attune pyromancies by resting at a bonfire.

Pyromancies can be purchased from Cornyx of the Great Swamp or Karla with the discovery of Pyromancy Tomes found in the game. Other pyromancies can be found as lootable items on corpses, inside of chests, by soul transposing various souls with Ludleth of Courland, or as rewards for ranking up in certain covenants.

title: Token of Fidelity
snippet: If the player is a member of the Blue Sentinels or Way of Blue covenants, they may trade a Token of Fidelity for a PvP sparring match in the Cathedral of Blue, near **The Blue Cathedral** bonfire.

title: Proof of a Concord Kept
snippet:
Proof of a Concord Kept -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Give to Captain Yorshka in Anor Londo to rank up in the Blade of the Darkmoon and Blue Sentinels covenants.

title: Miracle (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Miracle (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Miracles are aligned with Faith. To cast a miracle, a player requires a Talisman or Chime. There are also unique weapons that can act as a medium for casting miracles.

Miracles can be purchased from Irina of Carim or Karla with the discovery of Divine Braille Tomes found in game. Other miracles can be found as lootable items on corpses or inside of chests, or as covenant rewards and Soul Transposition results. Most miracles will focus on buffing or healing the player and allies in some way, while others will focus on inflicting either Lightning or Dark damage.

title: Equipment (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Equipment (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - belt_slot_items 
 belt_slot_items : Items can be placed in up to ten (10) belt slots. They are consumed, in order to restore stats or to counteract negative status effect. They can heal the player, cure curse, allow the player to gain souls, and more. They can also be covenant items, which will allow the player to rank up in different covenants when offered to the leader or shrine.

title: Boss (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Boss (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : **Bosses** are significant enemies in *Dark Souls III*. They usually control access to other areas throughout the game. Many bosses are mandatory for the completion of the main quest line, and some are optional.

Upon defeat, most bosses drop individual souls specific to themselves. These may be consumed or sold to acquire a large quantity of souls or may be transposed by Ludleth of Courland for weapons, shields, rings, miracles, pyromancies, or sorceries.

Once an area boss has been defeated, cooperation with friendly phantoms is disabled. However, the player will still be able to summon dark spirits and mad phantoms for PvP.

There are also minibosses in the game that do not respawn once killed. For the purposes of this wiki, those minibosses who drop a unique itemized soul are included in this article.

title: Player versus Player (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Player versus Player (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - counter_invasions 
 counter_invasions : Members of the Way of Blue can have a Blade of the Darkmoon or a member of the Blue Sentinels counter-invade their world when invaded by a player using a Cracked or whole Red Eye Orb. These players appear as a blue phantom. The Sentinels and Blades will counter-invade any invasion into a player's world by a red or purple (Mound-maker) phantom. However, if a purple phantom is summoned in by a White Sign Soapstone, neither the Sentinels nor Blades will counter-invade. The goal of these players is to slay the phantom. They will stay in the host's world so long as there is a hostile phantom present, excluding territory-defense covenants such as the Watchdogs of Farron. If the host reaches a fog gate with a Blade or Sentinel in their world, the blue phantom will be sent home along with the hostile invaders. The host cannot remove a blue phantom with the Black Separation Crystal.

title: Skeleton
snippet:
Skeleton -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Skeletons appear either as a patch of scattered bones that assemble when approached or already assembled and ready to fight. Their eye sockets glow with a white light, which make them easier to locate in darkened areas.

They wield either a Scimitar and Warrior's Round Shield, a Falchion and no shield, or a Longbow. Skeletons using the Scimitar or Falchion will inflict Bleed buildup with each of their attacks. Unlike many other enemies, skeletons can parry, riposte, and backstab.

In the graveyard at Firelink, their bones are scattered on the ground, and groups of them rise when the player character enters a specific space.

title: Humanity (gameplay mechanic)
snippet:
Humanity increases the power of Chaos weapons (up to 10 humanity)
Increases Curse resistance (up to 30 humanity)
Having Humanity in its soft form also allows you to use it to rank up in the Chaos Servant and Darkwraith Covenants.

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Brotherhood of Blood -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Invasions and duels in the Undead Purgatory are separated from one another, meaning that the player's rank will not level up from both invasions and duels. For instance, if a player with base rank has 25 dueling wins and 25 invasion kills, their rank will still remain at zero. Invasions with cracked red eye orbs do NOT count towards your total.
Losses in dueling or invasions will subtract one kill from the player's overall kill count for the respective area.
**If a player has 50 dueling wins and an equal amount of losses, their kill count will be zero.
**If a player has 50 dueling wins followed by 100 dueling losses, their kill count will be zero, not -50. It is not possible to achieve a negative overall kill count in the dueling arena.
Duels from a Red Sign Soapstone do not count towards your rank.
Killing Gren will automatically kick you out of the covenant.

title: Book of the Guilty
snippet:
Book of the Guilty -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Online play item. Check list of indicted players.

The Goddess of Sin Velka oversees this list of the guilty, who have disrespected the Gods or their covenants, and shall one day face the wrath of the Blades of the Darkmoon.

title: Human Effigy
snippet:
Human Effigy -  Dark Souls II - item - description 
 description : A warm, soft, shadow-like effigy.

Use this item to reverse Hollowing.
It also weakens the links to other worlds, preventing invasions and most cooperation.

Peer closely at an effigy, and one begins to perceive a human form, but whose form it takes depends on the person looking.

title: Agape Ring
snippet:
Agape Ring -  Dark Souls II - ring - use 
 use : The primary purpose of this ring is to lock Soul Memory at a specific matchmaking bracket for the purposes of PvP. By preventing the increase of Soul Memory, players are able to continue matchmaking at specific locations where lower-level players are more commonplace. This can be particularly useful for members of the Brotherhood of Blood covenant, who can continue invading in specific areas of the game regardless of game progress, or for members of the Heirs of the Sun covenant, who can continue to be summoned for specific areas and bosses without being pushed out of range by soul bounties.

title: Arbiter Spirit
snippet:
Arbiter Spirit -  Dark Souls II - enemy - rewards_for_killing_a_sinner 
 rewards_for_killing_a_sinner : If an Arbiter kills a sinner, they will be rewarded with a Token of Fidelity, which can be used to duel in the Blue Sentinel Arena in Heide's Tower of Flame. Arbiters receive no souls for killing their targets.

title: Chancellor Wellager
snippet:
After the Looking Glass Knight is defeated, he will begin selling new weapon variants that came included with the pre-ordered Black Armor edition of the game. Once NG++ is reached, Wellager will also sell all Covenant rewards of the Blue Sentinels and Brotherhood of Blood, allowing those who do not wish to grind the PVP-oriented covenants with no offline grinding method a way to still obtain that equipment. Note that increasing the bonfire intensity with Bonfire Ascetics won't work, and a proper NG+ playthrough must be initiated.

If the Giant Lord is defeated in the Memory of Jeigh, speaking to Wellager will have him gift the player with the Royal Dirk and the Espada Ropera, as well as the full Llewellyn Set in the Scholar of the First Sin edition of the game.

title: Smooth & Silky Stone
snippet:
Smooth & Silky Stone -  Dark Souls II - item - possible_trades 
 possible_trades : Upon trading with Dyna & Tillo, which is done by choosing the Leave option in your inventory while standing in their nest, one item from a set list will spawn on the ground. The possible rewards can be found on the Dyna & Tillo page.

title: Silver Knight Shield (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Unfortunately, it also loses out in many ways against the Lothric Knight Shield, which on top of being lighter and having higher stability also specializes in defending against Lightning damage. The only true advantage that the Silver Knight Shield has is that it requires less Strength to wield, making it more ideal on builds that attempt to limit their amount of Strength investment in favor of other stats.

title: Mound-makers
snippet:
Successfully completing an online session will reward the player with a Vertebra Shackle, which can be offered to the altar in the Pit of Hollows to rank up within the covenant. The method of entering the host's world has no effect on what the Mound-maker must do to complete the session.
